title: Customizing Claude Code: CLAUDE.md, Skills, Styles, and Permissions

questions.prompt: What size does Anthropic recommend for each CLAUDE.md file?
questions.explanation: Target under 200 lines per CLAUDE.md. Longer files consume more context and reduce adherence; move reference material into skills or path-scoped rules.

questions.prompt: Match each file location to who it applies to.

pairs.right: Everyone on the project, via git

questions.explanation: User files apply everywhere for you, project files are committed for the team, local files stay personal, and the shared settings file carries team permissions and hooks.

questions.prompt: To make a rule in .claude/rules/ load only for matching files, add ____ front-matter with glob patterns.
questions.explanation: Rules with paths front-matter load only when Claude works with matching files, saving context.

questions.prompt: Order how Claude Code evaluates permission rules.
questions.explanation: Rules are evaluated deny, then ask, then allow, and the first match wins, so an allow rule can't carve an exception out of a deny rule.

questions.prompt: Which statements about Claude Code skills are true? Select all that apply.

options.text: disable-model-invocation: true means only you can run the skill
$ARGUMENTS receives what you type after the command
A skill guarantees an action happens every time, like a hook

questions.explanation: Skills live in .claude/skills/, can be user-only via disable-model-invocation, and receive arguments through $ARGUMENTS. Skills are instructions; only hooks give guarantees.

questions.prompt: Which built-in output style leads with the result and drops preamble and recaps?
questions.explanation: Concise puts the result first and omits narration and recaps. Explanatory adds Insight blocks, Learning leaves TODO(human) pieces, and Proactive proceeds through routine decisions.
